title: How to Increase Dwell Time in Retail Stores | Entuned
meta_description: Practical strategies to keep customers browsing longer in your store, including how music tempo and mode directly control pace.

faq.q: How much does dwell time affect retail sales?
faq.a: Research has found that a 1% increase in dwell time correlates with approximately 1.3% increase in sales. The longer customers browse, the more products they see and the more likely they are to buy.

faq.q: Does music tempo really control how fast customers walk?
faq.a: Yes. Dr. Ronald Milliman's foundational study showed that customers walked significantly slower when slow-tempo music was playing and spent more because they encountered more products. This is one of the most replicated results in consumer behavior research, confirmed across retail formats.

faq.q: Why isn't tempo alone enough to increase dwell time?
faq.a: A 70 BPM track in a major key with bright, poppy production doesn't slow people down the same way as a 70 BPM track in a minor key with spacious production. Sparse, minor-key music at slow tempos produces the most pronounced dwell extension. Dense, major-key music at the same tempo produces almost none.

faq.q: How does music change how long customers feel they've been shopping?
faq.a: When customers enjoy the ambient environment, their perception of elapsed time compresses — twenty minutes of browsing feels like ten. The inverse is also true: mismatched or absent music makes time feel longer. Customers leave when they feel like they've been shopping long enough, and that feeling is subjective.
